newsitem.title: USA: Judge in Simpson trial removes only black juror.
newsitem.headline: Judge in Simpson trial removes only black juror.

text.p: The judge in O.J. Simpson's civil trial dismissed the only black member of the jury on Friday and ordered the panellists to begin their deliberations again.

A source involved in the trial said the dismissal of the woman -- identified as Rosemary Caraway -- after three days of deliberations, had nothing to do with an investigation into allegations of jury tampering that have swirled around the case this week.

The ex-football star, actor and television pitchman was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, by a criminal court jury in October 1995.
He is battling a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, who are seeking financial damages.

Caraway was removed for failing to disclose that her daughter was a legal secretary in the office of Los Angeles County District Attorney Gil Garcetti, who unsuccessfully prosecuted Simpson in the criminal case, the source said.
"She did say that her daughter was a legal secretary but didn't say who she worked for," the source said.

Caraway was replaced by an alternate juror, an Asian-American man in his 30s, a computer programmer who said during jury selection he was "neutral" but believed evidence planting was possible. The defence in the case has claimed evidence in the case was planted and contaminated.

The jury is now made up of six men and six women, among them nine whites, one Hispanic, one Asian-American and one man of mixed black and Asian descent. The panel that acquitted Simpson in his criminal trial was mostly black.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki, who has enforced a strict gag order throughout the case, on Friday called attorneys into his chambers to chastise them for leaking the identity of the dismissed juror and the reason she was booted off the panel.
And at the end of the day Fujisaki, apparently fearing a TV appearance by Caraway, asked the remaining jurors, who are not sequestered, to stay away from television, radio or newspapers.

"Sometimes in a long trial, because of the length of the trial and the inordinate amount of interest that apparently exists, things sometimes unravel," he said. "I'm trusting you to see that things do not unravel."
A spokeswoman for Garcetti said Fujisaki was informed by the District Attorney's Office on Thursday that Caraway's daughter worked in the office.
"We only learned yesterday afternoon that she was a sitting juror," the spokeswoman said. "We immediately communicated this information to the court."

Meanwhile, investigators continued to probe the jury tampering allegations, sparked earlier in the week by two jurors -- one of whom was the dismissed black panellist -- who informed Fujisaki that they had received a letter signed by two of the jurors in Simpson's criminal case.
The judge also turned down a demand by Robert Baker, Simpson's lead attorney, that a mistrial be declared.

In a hastily called court hearing to announce the juror's dismissal, Fujisaki said, "A juror has been excused for legal cause and replaced with an alternate juror ... The law grants each party in this case the right to a verdict reached only after full participation of all jurors who ultimately return the verdict."
"This right may be assured in this case only if the jury begins its deliberations again from the beginning," he said.

In the jury tampering probe, deputies from the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department on Thursday night searched the home of Brenda Moran, one of the criminal court jurors who signed the letter, and carted away a computer, note pads and other documents.

In another development on Friday, in a separate court, a family court judge refused to reconsider her earlier decision to award Simpson the custody of his young children, Sydney and Justin, whom he had with his slain ex-wife.
